title: Christmas Tree Lights and Decorations
strapline: A real tree, real decorations, and the moment we all switch the lights on together.
intent: Children explore how light is used at Christmas and take a genuine part in a festive tradition.
Hanging baubles and threading tinsel builds precise fine motor control.
Decorating a shared tree builds community, belonging and teamwork.
Switching the lights on together creates a shared moment children remember all year.
Children meet a tradition as participants rather than spectators.
implementation: Provide a small tree at child height with unbreakable baubles, tinsel and decorations.
Let children decide where each decoration goes, including when the result is lopsided.
Model safe handling of the lights and the tree, and talk about why we are careful.
Save the switch-on as a shared event with the whole room gathered and the lights off.
Talk about what Christmas lights mean to different families, including those who do not celebrate.
Keep a basket of decorations beside the tree so children can rearrange it all half-term.
Photograph the tree at each stage so children see what they built together.
key_questions: Where shall we hang this one so everyone can see it?
What happens to the room when we switch the lights on?
How should we hold the decorations to keep them safe?
What words describe how the tree looks — sparkly, glittering, glowing?
Does your family put lights up at home? What are they like?

impact.text: Children take part in a shared tradition and feel they belong to the group.
Children hang, thread and place decorations with precision and patience.
Children know that families and faiths celebrate differently, and that different is interesting.
Children use rich descriptive language about light and how it changes a room.
Children contribute to a group decision and keep to what was agreed.
Children ask real questions about the tradition and expect real answers.

enhancements: Child-made decorations — salt dough, paper chains, printed baubles — added to the bought ones.
A light table alongside with translucent baubles and coloured cellophane.
A countdown or advent routine where one thing changes each day.
A comparison of the tree with lamps and lanterns from other celebrations this half-term.
A photo book of the tree being decorated, kept in the book corner.
A "lights around the world" display of how different families light up a celebration.

playing_exploring: Children handle and investigate decorations, lights and textures freely.
The tree stays open all half-term for rearranging and revisiting.
active_learning: Children persist with fiddly hanging and threading until it holds.
They return to the tree repeatedly, adjusting and improving it.
creating_thinking: Children plan where a decoration should go and why.
They notice and reason about how light changes the look of the room.
